status: partial prepared implementation; not published or versioned as 1.72
finding: Shutdown admission counts an HTTP upgrade handler only until it returns. It did not impose a bound on complete WebSocket transport lifetimes or readers queued for retirement.
changes: Add a per-process connection gate before WebSocket upgrade. Default512; operator flag ws-max-connections accepts1–4096, with matching Compose environment and sample configuration. No live private environment was changed.
Include in-progress upgrades, anonymous/owned transports and closed readers awaiting the hub retirement handoff. Release failed upgrades immediately and retired readers exactly once.
At capacity refuse the new HTTP upgrade with503 and Retry-After:1, without creating queues, replacing existing owners or banning accounts/IPs. No role or forwarding claim bypasses this gate.

checks.concurrent: 128 concurrent attempts at a limit16 admit exactly16, remain held through all attempts, restore zero active slots on release and do not double-release. A zero-limit gate refuses admission.
checks.actualTransport: Production serveWs/readPump/writePump with loopback WebSockets and synthetic registration channels: failed origin reservation restores access; a successful upgrade holds the only slot after HTTP returns; a second upgrade gets503/Retry-After; closing TCP still retains its slot while the unbuffered retirement handoff waits; completing retirement restores ordinary upgrade. Two complete cycles pass.
checks.retainedBoundaries: Ping/pong/data shared budget, normal keepalives, shutdown refusal and real origin checks remain passing.

limits: 512 is a resource ceiling, not a measured player-capacity or beta promise. Unit concurrency is not a128-real-player workload.

Synthetic registration channels isolate real transport admission, not authenticated Mongo/session/save/graceful-restart behavior; later exact-source integration and CI/public acceptance remain required.

Pre-header TCP sockets, connection attempts per second, upstream bandwidth, global network attacks and malicious occupation of available slots still need edge/workload review. No IP-ban policy or production nginx/firewall change is implied.
Broader movement/cast, private-message/event visibility, secret exposure and recovery decisions remain separate unfinished milestone work.
